analysis.title: GS Housing Market Activity Scale: Week of November 8: Scale Up 2% Sequentially as Rates Move Off Their Recent Peak
key_insights: GS housing activity scale for the week of November 8 rose 2% sequentially but was down 14% YOY, 33% below the long-term average. The weekly scale remains at 3.

The sequential gain was led by a 7% increase in mortgage purchase applications and an improvement in median listing price. Sales, homes off market in two weeks, and median new listing and sale prices each deteriorated by 1%.
The 30-year mortgage rate fell 7bps to 7.11% (Freddie Mac), up 87bps YOY.
GS channel checks suggest housing activity has remained weak in November, reflecting macro uncertainty and rate volatility.
GS is focused on homebuilders with company-specific initiatives, including potential capital allocation, and highlights Buy-rated IBP.
If conditions for builders improve, GS sees the greatest upside in MTH and DHI because of their entry-level exposure and disciplined balance of margins and uses of cash.

Positive indicators: active listings up 3% YOY (3% below the 2019 average), sale-to-list ratio of 98.2% (35bps above the same week in 2019), time on market two days below the same week in 2019, and 26% of homes off market within 2 weeks vs 25% in 2019.
Weak indicators: median sale price down 1% YOY (Redfin), median list price down 1% YOY, and home sales down 9% YOY and 1% sequentially.
Mortgage applications fell 39% YOY (vs -42% the prior week). Refinancings fell 57% YOY (vs -60%) and purchase applications fell 18% YOY (vs -20%).
Purchase applications are 9% above the mid-October trough and 4% above the October average. GS expects activity to stay under pressure given the macro backdrop.
ARMs were 11% of application volume, down 50bps sequentially and vs 8% a year ago.

market_movers.rationale: GS highlights IBP as its preferred name given company-specific initiatives, including potential capital allocation. Rating and price cited as Buy, $229.00.
GS sees the greatest upside to MTH if builder conditions improve, given entry-level exposure and a disciplined approach to margins and cash use. Rating and price cited as Buy, $64.47.
GS sees the greatest upside to DHI if builder conditions improve, given entry-level exposure and a disciplined approach to margins and cash use. Rating and price cited as Buy, $145.55.

sector_views.rationale: Activity remains weak and GS expects it to stay under pressure on macro uncertainty. GS favors names with company-specific initiatives and sees upside only if conditions improve.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Down 7bps sequentially and up 87bps YOY. The decline lifted purchase applications.
Improved from -20% the prior week, up 7% sequentially, but still below last year.
Up 2% sequentially, off 14% YOY, 33% below the long-term average. A reading of 5 is in line with historical norms.
Monthly reading is above the weekly reading but still below the long-term average of 5.

risk_factors: Macro uncertainty and rate volatility are keeping housing activity weak in November.
Affordability concerns and the economic backdrop are leading to buyer hesitancy.
Purchase application gains may not hold if rates rise again.

tension_points.bull_case: Falling rates lifted purchase applications 7% sequentially. Listings, sale-to-list ratio, time on market and off-market share are at or better than 2019 levels. GS sees potential for greater activity if headwinds abate.
tension_points.bear_case: Sales are down 9% YOY, median sale and list prices are down 1% YOY, and the scale is 33% below its long-term average. GS channel checks show weak activity in November and GS expects activity to stay under pressure on the macro backdrop.
